testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Beetle-control logging and grazing rights abuses at Klamath Reservation
testimony.key_claims: Zimmerman's letter to Senator Steiwer stated less than 25% merchantable timber with rest bug-infested; trees marked for cutting were left standing; timber sold too cheaply. General council adopted resolution to sell grazing rights to highest bidder but Crawford allowed Crystal to bring sheep onto reservation before ranches were advertised for bid. Crawford was instrumental in removing sheep and then returning them under guise of Indian ownership through conditional-sales contracts with sisters-in-law and wife's nephew. Engle sold 500 head of sheep each to mother and sister without right to do so. Kirk requests thorough investigation into violation of Act 435 and asks committee to request Weaver's report on beetle-control logging.

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Appeals to Commissioner of Indian Affairs
testimony.key_claims: Tribe has appealed to Commissioner in person and in writing and in every way possible without satisfactory response.

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States (written statement)
testimony.subject: Indian Court of Claims bill and legal representation dispute
testimony.key_claims: In 1922 F.G. Collett threatened Indians who did not subscribe to Indian Board of Cooperation would be left off rolls. In 1925 Tuolumne auxiliary held joint meeting with Eureka Indians; Collett failed to answer questions about funds and statements; auxiliary discontinued relations with board. Claims that 17,000 Indians voted to hire Henderson Pemberton & Hanley is in error because Me-wuk section of Calaveras, Tuolumne, and parts of Mariposa Counties had no voice or representative at those meetings. Me-wuk Tribe flatly refuses to accept Henderson Pemberton & Hanley as representatives. Tribe supports Attorney General U.S. Webb and will contest any fee allowed to the rejected law firm.
